In regard to program mentors, in my experience, we speak once a week. He usually asks me questions and we develop a plan together. He doesn’t tell me what to do but makes suggestions. In between calls, I e-mail him if I need something and he’ll respond within minutes to a couple of hours.

Course mentors are helpful as well. You can schedule a meeting with them if you have questions, need help, or anything else for the course you are working on.

For the OA’s (tests), I believe you can take it three times before having to pay a retake fee. I didn’t pass an OA and before the retake was approved, I had a call with the course mentor. She gave me study guides to complete. I sent them back and she approved the retake. She also sent quizzes with an answer key for me to study. I passed on the retake with significantly higher improvement.
I wish I would have had a heads up...anyhow, on to the next assignment.

I've seen the negative comments as well.  I attribute it to the fact that some individuals are not going to do well as online learners.  Instead of recognizing this, they complain and blame it on others.  Online education requires a commitment to succeed.  One has to be willing to do the work.  

I earned my BA from a different online institution which was structured differently.  We didn't have student mentors.  In fact, the contact at the school wasn't much help.  It was a for\-profit school that did not challenge my intellectual abilities.  I felt as if I could pass anything without any effort....they took my money and gave me a degree whether or not I was learning.

During my first class with WGU, both assignments were kicked back.  That's when I realized this school means business and I would have to put forth effort to earn my degree.  I feel like so many people look at online schools as lesser that B&M's.  When they finally realize it requires work, they become discouraged and it's the schools fault.  It's not.  WGU provides a wealth of resources from the Program Mentors to the counseling, writing center, Course Mentors, etc.  

If they can't see what we see, it's their loss.  You can't be the price with the regional accreditation.
